lines: Oh. Hello.
Not many people walk out this far.
You're not from the town, are you?
0.note: A woman by the path. Polite, a little guarded.

reply: Outside town. The path takes you back.
Follow it west. No, east. East.

lines: Hello again, {player}.
Still walking? Good. Most people drive.
1.note: Sigrún remembers you.

lines: The lake? Colder than it looks.
People swim in it in summer. I don't.
1.note: Sigrún: the lake is cold. People swim in it in summer.

lines: Someone built it so the path can be found in fog.
Don't knock it over. People still use them.
1.note: Sigrún: stone piles mark the path in fog. Don't knock them over.

lines: Morning.
Mind the ropes there.
0.note: A fisherman coiling rope. Busy, not unfriendly.

lines: {player}. Back again.
The sea was kind today. Small mercies.
1.note: Gunnar nods at you. He remembers your name.

lines: She's older than me, near enough.
My father fished from her. Now I do.
1.note: Gunnar: his boat belonged to his father.

lines: That's how we dry fish. Just wind and cold air.
Dried fish with butter. Best snack there is.
1.note: Gunnar: fish is dried on racks by the wind. Eaten with butter.

lines: Good day.
Stay back from the edge, please.
0.note: A woman with a clipboard. She watches everything.

choices.text: We just moved in. I'll be careful!

lines: Hello, {player}.
Quiet day. I like quiet days.
1.note: Halldóra gives you a small smile.

lines: The wall keeps the big waves out.
In a winter storm, you'll see why we need it.
1.note: Halldóra: the harbour wall keeps out big waves.

lines: I know every boat here, and who sails it.
Fish is a big part of how this country earns.
1.note: Halldóra: fish is one of Iceland's biggest exports.

lines: Hello. We open early.
Everything on the left is from this morning.
0.note: A baker with flour on her sleeves. Polite, a little busy.

choices.text: We're new in town. It smells amazing!
reply: Welcome. Tell your family we're here.

lines: {player}! Good morning.
I saved the last bun. Don't tell anyone.
1.note: Ásta waves when you come in.

lines: My grandmother sang in that church.
On Christmas Eve, half the town goes. I bake all week.
1.note: Ásta: half the town goes to church on Christmas Eve.

lines: Hot water from the ground heats our homes.
Some people even bake rye bread in hot earth.
1.note: Ásta: rye bread can be baked slowly in hot ground.

lines: Who are you?
Why are you looking at everything?
Is that your real hair?
0.note: A kid in a yellow coat. Stares at you a lot.

choices.text: We just moved here. I'm new!
reply: Do you like fish? Everyone here likes fish.

lines: {player}! Where were you?
Did you know you walk funny?
Not bad funny. Just funny.
1.note: Kári is pleased to see you. Very pleased.

lines: Why is the door never locked?
Mamma says nobody steals from a church.
Would you? I wouldn't. Probably.
1.note: Kári: the church door is never locked.

lines: In September the sheep come down from the hills.
Everyone helps sort them. Why don't sheep get lost?
Do you have sheep where you're from?
1.note: Kári: sheep come down from the hills in September.

lines: Hello.
Don't climb on anything here. It's hot.
0.note: A man in an orange work jacket. Polite, careful.

reply: Welcome. Is your house warm enough?
If not, it's probably the valves.
It's where the hot water comes from.
Well, it comes from the ground. We just move it.

lines: Hi, {player}.
Long shift. Good to see a friendly face.
1.note: Einar remembers you.

lines: That pipe carries water heated deep underground.
Most homes in Iceland are heated that way.
1.note: Einar: most Icelandic homes are heated with hot water from underground.

smell.label: Ask why the tap water smells

lines: The eggy smell? That's sulphur from the ground.
Only the hot tap. The cold water is clean and fresh.
1.note: Einar: hot tap water can smell of sulphur. Cold water does not.

lines: Hello.
Close the gate behind you, if you came through it.
0.note: A farmer in a thick wool jumper. Watches you closely.

choices.text: We just moved here. I closed it!

reply: The rest think they own me.

lines: {player}. You again.
Gates closed? Good.
1.note: Hrafnhildur almost smiles.

lines: In summer the sheep roam free in the hills.
In September we gather them and sort them here.
1.note: Hrafnhildur: sheep roam free all summer. In September they are gathered and sorted.

lines: My grandfather stacked stones on that path.
He walked it to church every Sunday. In any weather.
1.note: Hrafnhildur: her grandfather walked the old path to church.
